security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel enables the Smip/Smaclic fast interrupt extension but does not save, restore, or sanitize the SIPU bit in sstatus across context switches. When a thread is rescheduled with SIPU inadvertently set (inherited from firmware, a previous privilege level, or a misconfigured bhyve guest), any subsequent supervisor interrupt trap triggers hardware automatic stacking that the kernel's trap entry path does not expect, corrupting the trap frame layout.
security_spec.summary: SIPU/MIPU bits in sstatus/mstatus control automatic interrupt stacking; FreeBSD must clear SIPU on boot and ensure sstatus is sanitized per-thread, or hardware stacking corrupts trap frames during interrupt delivery

findings.finding: Trap entry captures the raw hardware sstatus value (including all WPRI bits) into the trapframe via 'csrr t0, sstatus; sd t0, (TF_SSTATUS)(sp)' without masking any undefined/reserved bits. Trap return restores the full tf_sstatus value back to hardware via 'csrw sstatus, t0', only toggling SIE/SPIE but leaving all other bits (including future SIPU encoding at an as-yet-unallocated bit position) unchanged. If SIPU were ever set (by firmware, a hypervisor, or future hardware), the bit would persist in tf_sstatus across the entire trap round-trip and propagate to subsequent context switches.
findings.snippet:
csrr    t0, sstatus
sd      t0, (TF_SSTATUS)(sp)
...
ld      t0, (TF_SSTATUS)(sp)
csrw    sstatus, t0

spec_citations.excerpt: If MIPU, is set, a trap taken at Machine level due to an interrupt causes automatic stacking. If SIPU, is set, a trap taken at Supervisor level due to an interrupt causes automatic stacking. ... NOTE: These bits do not yet have an allocated encoding. The authors of this specification intend to ask for encoding of these bits in mstatus/sstatus.
sstatus register diagram for SXLEN=64: bits between SPP and FS are marked WPRI (Write Preserved, Reads Ignored). Bit 9 is currently WPRI.

findings.finding: fork_trampoline restores sstatus from the trapframe for a newly forked process, only masking SIE before writing back via 'csrw sstatus, t0'. The fork path (cpu_fork in vm_machdep.c) does a raw bcopy of the parent's entire trapframe, propagating any SIPU bit value from parent to child. No sanitization of undefined/WPRI bits occurs at any point in the fork-to-first-userspace-return chain.
findings.snippet:
ld      t0, (TF_SSTATUS)(sp)
li      t1, ~SSTATUS_SIE
and     t0, t0, t1
csrw    sstatus, t0

spec_citations.excerpt: If SIPU, is set, a trap taken at Supervisor level due to an interrupt causes automatic stacking.

findings.finding: cpu_fork copies the parent's entire trapframe (including tf_sstatus) to the child via bcopy(), then only modifies SPIE and SPP bits. Any SIPU bit set in the parent's tf_sstatus is inherited by the child without inspection or sanitization. This means a SIPU bit introduced at any point (firmware, hypervisor, kernel bug) would silently propagate across fork() to all child processes.

set_mcontext validates sstatus changes from userspace via sigreturn, but the exclusion mask (~SSTATUS_SD | SSTATUS_XS_MASK | SSTATUS_FS_MASK | SSTATUS_UPIE | SSTATUS_UIE) does not exclude WPRI bits (including the future SIPU bit position). Userspace can modify these bits through signal context manipulation, and the value is written directly to tf->tf_sstatus, which will later be restored to hardware sstatus on trap return.

spec_citations.excerpt: sstatus bit layout shows multiple WPRI fields. WPRI bits must be preserved by software but are ignored by hardware.

findings.finding: SSTATUS_* macro definitions are incomplete: no SSTATUS_SIPU (bit 9) definition exists, and no SSTATUS_WPRI_MASK is defined that would allow the trap entry/exit and context switch code to sanitize reserved bits. Without a WPRI mask, any code path that writes sstatus must either enumerate all defined bits or risk inadvertently setting future architecturally-defined bits.

spec_citations.excerpt: sstatus for SXLEN=64: WPRI bits at positions 2-3, 9, 11-12, 19-31, 34-62 (with UXL at 32-33). These bits must be preserved on write.

findings.finding: KASSERT checks on trap entry validate SPP, SIE, and SUM bits. These are reasonable correctness checks that do catch common corruptions. No SIPU check is possible since the bit encoding is not yet allocated. This is correct behavior for the current ISA state.
findings.snippet:
KASSERT((csr_read(sstatus) & (SSTATUS_SPP | SSTATUS_SIE)) ==
    SSTATUS_SPP, ("Came from S mode with interrupts enabled"));
